newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine flour firms may buy wheat - trade.
newsitem.headline: Philippine flour firms may buy wheat - trade.

text.p: Philippine flour companies may place a few orders for wheat this week with purchases this year expected to remain brisk, traders said on Monday.
Traders said they expected local flour millers to buy between 1.8 million and 2.1 million tonnes of wheat in 1997.
"We may see some orders this week, but as to how big I don't know," said one trader.
The local wheat market has been quiet in the past two weeks due to the long Christmas holiday period.
Philippine flour millers imported an estimated 1.85 million to 1.9 million tonnes of wheat, largely from the United States, in 1996, versus 2.4 million tonnes imported in 1995.
"Hopefully, the market should recover with more alternative (sources) this year," an official in one of the country's largest flour mills told Reuters.
But another trader said he expected wheat imports to remain almost steady from last year's figures as firms were seen importing more corn for animal feed in 1997.
"Some wheat importations in the past years were being used as feed," he said.
The Philippines buys its wheat largely from the United States. "We expect orders from other countries like Australia and Canada to pick up this year," he said.
Reports of crop damage in Argentina, howver, may push up wheat prices. "Quality of Argentine wheat might also suffer," said another trader.

Traders attributed the drop in the country's wheat imports last year to higher prices in the United States and an uproar over the use of potassium bromate in making small fluffy bread called pan de sal.
Reports in the local media that the bread might contain high quantities of potassium bromate, which is said to be carcinogenic in large doses, led to a fall in demand for bakery goods.
Ric Pinca of the Philippine Association of Flour Millers said there is no evidence that use of potassium bromate in small quantities causes cancer.

The Department of Trade and Industry said the price of hard flour, which is used in making bread, was steady at 290 pesos per 25 kg bag this week, while the price of soft flour, used in making cakes and pastries, was also unchanged at 260 pesos.

Philippine Agriculture Secretary Salvador Escudero said he expected the country to import between 300,000 to 500,000 tonnes of rice this year and up to 500,000 tonnes of corn due to a projected shortfall in production.
The Department of Agriculture is scheduled to release the country's year-end rice and corn inventories this week, and projected rice and corn production forecast in the first half of 1997.
"The year-end forecast will be used to determine the actual volume of the country's rice and corn importations this year," an official said.
Traders said the average retail price of white corn was steady at 11.88 pesos per kg and yellow corn at 10.72 pesos per kg.
